_comment: Hand-placed map markers — the positions are OURS, not the wiki's, and
every record built from this file ships inferred and renders hollow.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The wiki map publishes 46 markers and none of them
is a dig site or Balor's wagon, which are exactly the pins players ask
for. No source anywhere states a coordinate for either — dig spots are
rolled onto random tiles each day, and the wagon has no wiki marker — so
the only honest way onto the map is a human placing a pin and saying so.
That is what `inferred` means on a spot and `anchor_inferred` on a
location: the THING is real and stated, the POSITION is our judgement.
DIG SPOTS. Which areas have dig sites is derived, not curated: the
builder takes every location where a shipped artifact window uses method
dig_spot, and this file supplies only the x/y for the overworld ones. A
coordinate here for an area the data says has no digging fails the
build — this file must never be the source of WHERE digging exists, only
of where the pin sits. Each area gets ONE marker: the game spawns
several spots per area at random positions daily, and no source states
how many, so several pins would be an invented count in invented places.
The app says 'random spots daily' on the pin instead.
The five mine biomes and the_mines also carry dig windows and get no
marker: a biome is a range of floors with no overworld position (that is
not-applicable, not unknown), and the mines' digging renders on the
mines screen.
PLACEMENT. Coordinates are SVG user units in the world map's viewBox,
like every other coordinate. Each was picked as the centre-most cell of
the region's measured footprint that is not on top of the region's own
anchor — so a pin is guaranteed inside its region and clear of the
label, and claims nothing finer than 'somewhere in this area', which is
the truth.
BALOR'S WAGON. The game's own room file (tiled/rooms/Town/rm_town.tmx)
places a wagon object in town — the wagon has a fixed pitch, contrary to
what curated/aliases/map_markers.json used to guess. Its map position
here is hand-placed near the town square and is approximate.

anchors.reason: Balor's travelling shop has a fixed pitch in town — rm_town.tmx places the wagon object — but no wiki marker. Placed by hand beside the town square, inside Mistria's measured footprint.

dig_spots.reason: Shipped artifact windows dig in town. Pin sits centre-of-footprint, clear of the town anchor.
